data.title: Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) peel
data.summary: Non-neutralised peel graded by frost; superficial use and TCA CROSS for scars
data.body:
Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) coagulates epidermal proteins and produces a visible **frost**. Depth depends on concentration, number of coats, how much is applied and how the skin is prepared. It does not need neutralising, and it is not systemically toxic. Concentrations of 10–25% act superficially. At 35% and above it reaches the papillary dermis (medium depth), and in skin types IV–V scarring and PIH become real risks.

## Indications
- Superficial (10–20%): melasma, PIH, lentigines, fine lines, superficial acne scars
- Medium-depth (35%, usually combined with Jessner's or GA): rarely used in Indian skin; consider only after careful selection
- **TCA CROSS** (70–100%, focal): ice-pick and narrow boxcar acne scars
- Focal: xanthelasma, seborrhoeic keratoses (experienced hands only)

## Contraindications
- Active infection or dermatitis at the site, open wounds
- Keloid or hypertrophic scar tendency
- Isotretinoin in the past 6 months (deeper peels)
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding
- Previous radiotherapy at the site, poor wound healing
- Inability to follow sun protection and aftercare

## Pre-procedure
- Written consent: visible peeling for 5–7 days, PIH, scarring and hypopigmentation
- **Priming 2–4 weeks** with tretinoin and hydroquinone; this is essential in skin types IV–V
- Antiviral prophylaxis for perioral and full-face peels
- Test spot with the planned concentration
- Baseline photographs

## Equipment
- Freshly made TCA in the required w/v concentration, in labelled amber bottles
- Cotton-tipped applicators (moist, not dripping), gauze
- For CROSS: wooden toothpick or fine applicator
- Degreaser, petrolatum, cold compresses, fan

## Procedure step by step
1. Cleanse and degrease thoroughly; uneven degreasing gives patchy frost.
2. Protect the eyes; apply petrolatum to the alae, commissures and canthi.
3. Apply TCA one cosmetic unit at a time, with even strokes.
4. Wait 2–3 minutes after each coat; frost develops slowly. Add a further coat only where the frost is short of the target.
5. **Endpoints by frost level**:
- Level I: erythema with scattered speckles of frost (superficial; the usual goal in skin types IV–V)
- Level II: white frost with pink showing through (upper papillary dermis)
- Level III: solid opaque white frost (deeper; avoid in brown skin except focal CROSS)
6. Apply cool compresses for comfort. No neutralisation is needed.
7. **TCA CROSS**: press the sharpened applicator into the base of each pitted scar for a few seconds, until the scar turns white. Do not treat adjacent normal skin.

## Post-procedure care
- Skin darkens and peels on days 3–7; do not pick
- Bland ointment or moisturiser, gentle cleanser, strict photoprotection
- Restart priming agents only after peeling is complete

## Complications & management
- PIH: common in skin types IV–V; hydroquinone, sunscreen, delay further peels
- Persistent erythema beyond 3 weeks: suspect impending scarring and start a potent topical steroid early
- Hypertrophic scarring: intralesional steroid, silicone gel
- Infection (bacterial, candida, herpes): swab and treat promptly
- Hypopigmentation or demarcation lines: feather the edges at the jawline

## Sessions & follow-up
- Superficial TCA every 3–4 weeks for 3–4 sessions
- TCA CROSS every 4–6 weeks for 3–6 sessions
- Review at day 7 after the first peel
